property_summary: For every input where the external low-level call to caddress returns success, the reference contract C always returns true from transfer (and never returns false); the mutant inverts that check and can return false when the external call succeeds, so there exist inputs (a callee that succeeds) that make the mutant return false while the reference still returns true.

For any inputs where transfer completes (does not revert), the reference C always returns true; the mutant can return false when the external caddress.call succeeds (mutant inverted the success check).

For every input where the callee (caddress) call succeeds, reference C.transfer always returns true; the mutant inverts the success check and can return false when the callee call succeeds, so there exists an adversarial callee that succeeds causing the mutant to differ while the reference still returns true.

For any non-empty _tos array and matching v array, C.transfer always returns true after completing all calls (does not return early); the mutant that moves the return into the loop may return after the first iteration for multi-recipient calls, so for some inputs the observed return differs.

For any non-empty array of recipients and matching values, the correct contract always returns true (completes all internal calls) for the full call; the mutant may return after the first successful internal call causing the external call to still return true but without performing subsequent calls — we detect this by observing that when the callee succeeds for the first recipient but reverts for a later recipient, the correct contract call reverts while the mutant returns true (does not propagate the later revert).

For any non-empty list of recipients and values where the callee succeeds for the first recipient but may revert for a later recipient, the reference C always propagates a later revert (so the overall call reverts), whereas the mutant that returns inside the loop can return true after the first successful call and thus mask later reverts; the test deploys a helper that succeeds once then reverts to detect this difference.

For any non-empty list of recipients, if the called external contract may succeed for the first recipient and revert for a later recipient, the reference C always propagates that later revert (so the transfer call reverts), while the mutant that returns inside the loop can return true after the first success and thus fail to propagate a later revert.

For any non-empty recipient list and matching value list, C.transfer either completes all internal calls (returning true) or reverts if any internal call later fails; the mutant that returns inside the loop can return true after the first successful call and thus may not revert even if a later internal call would fail — so the property: if the callee reverts for any recipient position > 0 while succeeding for position 0, then the reference C.transfer reverts (ok==false) but the mutant may return true (ok==true).

For any nonempty list of recipients and matching amounts, calling transfer as the authorized sender causes C to always forward amounts scaled by 1e18 to the external caddress (so the cumulative forwarded amount equals sum(v[i] * 1e18)); the mutant removing the 1e18 multiplier breaks this by forwarding unscaled amounts for some fuzzed v values.

For any non-empty arrays of recipients and amounts called by the authorized sender, the correct contract always forwards (via low-level call) the amounts scaled by 1e18 causing the callee to receive a call that succeeds; the mutant removing the 1e18 scaling will cause differing call behavior for some fuzzed amount values (the rule: calls succeed for scaled amounts), which the mutant can break.

For any non-empty arrays of recipients and matching positive uint amounts invoked by the authorized sender, the reference C always makes the low-level call to caddress with the amount multiplied by 1e18 (so the callee receives a calldata encoding whose last 32-byte word equals v[i]*1e18 for each entry); the mutant that removes the 1e18 multiplier will cause the calldata last word to instead equal v[i]*1 for some fuzzed v, so comparing the observed calldata payload read back from a helper callee distinguishes them.

For any non-empty arrays and any caller, C always forwards the third parameter in each transferFrom call as v[i] multiplied by 1e18 (so a helper callee observing calldata will see v[i]*1e18), whereas the mutant removes the 1e18 multiplier causing the observed calldata last word to sometimes differ.

For every non-empty arrays of recipients and amounts called by the authorized sender and for any callee address that echoes back the received calldata, C always forwards the third argument as v[i] multiplied by 1e18 (so the echoed calldata contains v[i]*1e18), whereas the mutant that removed the 1e18 multiplier will cause the echoed calldata to contain v[i]*1 for some fuzzed v and thus differ.

For every call to transfer by the authorized sender with arrays of equal positive length, the reference contract forwards an amount equal to v[i] * 1e18 to caddress for each i; the mutant instead sometimes forwards v[i] + 1e18, so the total/each forwarded amount can differ — making the forwarded amount equality rule fail for some fuzzed v[i].

For every input arrays and caller equal to the authorized address, the reference contract forwards an amount exactly equal to v[i] * 1e18 for each index i (so the sum of forwarded amounts equals sum(v)*1e18); the mutant instead uses v[i] + 1e18, breaking this equality for some fuzzed v values.

For any caller and input arrays (with length>0) when the authorized sender calls transfer through a callee that records the forwarded amounts, the reference contract always forwards amounts equal to v[i]*1e18 for each index; the mutant forwards v[i]+1e18 for some inputs, breaking equality for those inputs.

For any caller equal to the authorized address and any non-empty arrays, the reference forwards to caddress amounts exactly equal to v[i] * 1e18 for every index i (the mutant sometimes forwards v[i] + 1e18), so the recorded forwarded amounts must equal v[i]*1e18 for all i — the mutant breaks this for some v.

For any caller equal to the authorized address and any non-empty arrays, the correct contract always calls caddress with each amount equal to v[i] * 1e18; the mutant instead uses v[i] + 1e18 for some v, so recording the forwarded amounts reveals a mismatch for some fuzzed v inputs.
